headline: Less parallel. Less wasteful. Efficiency unproven.

causal_interpretation.primary: The successor had a narrower runnable graph: only P1-10 had completed grilling, while P1-04, P1-05, P1-06, P1-07, and P1-11 remained needs-interview.
secondary: Three reusable architecture, review, and writer threads occupied the spawned-agent limit and blocked otherwise useful lightweight or independent work.
The 1.50 GiB heavy-operation memory floor created a volatile admission cliff close to otherwise runnable gates.
causal_interpretation.not_supported: The evidence does not support treating machine admission as the dominant cause of the parallelism decline.

efficiency_interpretation.conclusion: The wall-clock token-rate reduction mostly tracks reduced worker activity. Accepted-work-per-token or accepted-work-per-quota efficiency is not established by this snapshot.

quota_interpretation: Quota consumption is not an orchestration throttle. Faster quota use is acceptable when it buys useful accepted work, especially near resets; the workflow must not introspect or schedule around subscription quota.
polling_interpretation: The nearly unchanged wait_agent rate is a weak headline metric. Root-owned external CI polling caused by the unavailable monitor slot is actionable; generic event-wait cadence is not evidence of inefficiency by itself.

evidence: After R1 froze shared contracts, R2a and R2b were the first explicitly concurrent-ready siblings, but they were scheduled sequentially because the three reusable spawned-agent threads occupied the available limit.
A 2026-08-31T22:05:39.2671979Z admission sample found 1.48 GiB available memory and denied the queued R2b heavy gate against the 1.50 GiB floor.
The architecture lead was retained as recallable while subsequent artifact reviews repeatedly reported that no architecture recall was required.
post_cutoff_addendum.use: This addendum sharpens hypotheses for the next evaluation but is excluded from the preserved cutoff metrics.
